chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from 'Uthman ibn Sa'id from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about the earnings of the female singer and the female wailer, and he disliked it.

key_terms.النَّائِحَة: The female professional wailer (one who mourns loudly)
key_terms.فَكَرِهَهُ: And he disliked it (indicating makruh status in fiqh)
key_terms.كَسْب: Earnings or income derived from work or profession

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on the earnings of female singers and mourners?
ai.summary: Transmitted through the reliable chain of al-Tusi’s Tahdhib, this narration records Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) ruling on the earnings of female singers and professional mourners, deeming them makruh (disliked). This classification reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that while their income is not strictly haram, it is tainted by the nature of their profession, which often involves frivolity or mourning rituals contrary to Islamic decorum. The ruling underscores the importance of the source of income in Islamic ethics, linking professional conduct to spiritual purity.
